newsitem.title: FINLAND: Forestries to boost Helsinki, Nokia may rise more.
newsitem.headline: Forestries to boost Helsinki, Nokia may rise more.

text.p: Forestry stocks were expected to boost the Helsinki bourse after a 6.27 percent rise in the Standard & Poors U.S. paper stocks index, and Nokia may extend gains on Motorola's Q2 report, operators said.
"I think the bourse will rise clearly," one analyst said, pointing to the forestry gains the U.S. "The overall trend will be up about one percent," said one broker. Others saw even sharper gains.
Motorola reported second quarter earnings per share at 62 cents excluding extraordinary items, versus a 56 cent average estimate, which was seen boosting Motorola, and possibly Nokia.
Operators said Nokia may test 420.00 markka in Helsinki near term after closing at the equivalent of about 416 markka on Wall Street. Reaching 420 would be a one percent advance.
"There are such good vibes that I don't expect any profit-taking (in Nokia) yet, we think it will continue rising," a broker said.

Among paper stocks, one broker said forestry major UPM would trade at new record levels above 130 markka on Wednesday, which would be up at least 1.7 percent on Tuesday. "I don't expect to see anything below 130," he said.
